exports.text: General hypercall takes control plus optional input and output buffers, uses zero address for absent buffers, invokes the hypervisor and returns status; narrow builds without mapped page report all ones.

Fast hypercalls form control from code plus fast flag and pass one or two register values with no buffers, returning status; wide builds use indirect static dispatch, narrow builds use the mapped page.
Assist accessor returns per-processor assist page or null when absent, with always-null fallback; fallback flush and APIC translation report failure, MSR getters return zero and setters discard.
Synthetic controller test checks a register interval and channel test checks its subrange; raw read delegates to native read and NMI reason returns zero here.
APIC init, MMU setup, protocol negotiation, early VTL init and VTL return are no-ops or constants here; flush-list filler is a function pointer returning integer status.

hazards.text: Callers must handle absent support: unmapped narrow hypercall yields all ones, assist may be null, fallback flush and translation fail, and MSR getters return zero while setters ignore input.
Wide dispatch relies on external static-call helper and narrow splitting on external low and high half extractors owned elsewhere.

invariants.text: Multiprocessor tables use fixed four-character signatures with checksums making unsigned byte sum zero; lengths give size and unused and reserved fields are zero.

structs.text: Floating pointer holds signature, table address, length in paragraphs, version, checksum and feature bytes for config state and interrupt mode; header holds signature, length, revision, checksum, vendor and product identity, vendor table size, APIC address and reserved field.
Entry types are small ordered integers for processor, bus, IOAPIC, interrupt source and local source, with a separate high value for translation.

Processor entry holds type, APIC ids and version, flags, features and reserved words with single-bit enabled and boot flags and nibble masks for family model stepping; bus entry holds type, id and six-character name.
Bus types use short uppercase names; usable IOAPIC is shown by the low flag bit.

IOAPIC entry holds type, id, version, flags and address; interrupt source holds type, kind, flags, source bus and line plus destination controller and line, with maskable, NMI, SMI and external kinds, two-bit polarity and trigger fields with masks, and all-ones broadcast.

Local source parallels interrupt source with bus and local input ids; vendor table has signature, length, revision, checksum and identifier with underscore-OEM mark; simple bus order is ISA then EISA then PCI.
Hypervisor IOAPIC base is a fixed high address; trust levels are zero normal, one secure and two management; secondary start uses fixed page attributes and all-ones segment limit.
Trust-level CPU context shows general registers as named fields and as sixteen-entry array, followed by floating and vector state.
Message data packs vector, delivery mode, logical destination flag, level, trigger and reserved bits with alternate remapping subhandle view and architecture alias.
Low message address packs mode, hint, destination parts and base bits; high address carries upper destination; bases reflect local APIC range with high part zero.
Supported vector MSI flags add MSI-X and dynamic allocation to generic mask; required flags demand default domain and chip operations.

Architectural registers cover extended features, call targets and mask, FS and GS bases, kernel GS base and TSC aux; enable masks select call support, long mode, NX, virtualization, segment limit, fast save restore, translation extensions and automatic branch control.

Memory types encode uncacheable, combining, through, protected, back and weak uncacheable; fixed MTRRs cover low memory with 64K, 16K and 4K registers plus default type, and page attribute packs eight type bytes.

Test, speculation-control and prediction registers provide split-lock, branch-restriction, store-bypass and barrier controls with combined mitigations mask; architecture capabilities report immunity and presence for meltdown, branch, store-bypass, sampling and abort classes.

Core capabilities also cover branch-history, return-stack, gather, register-file and target-selection properties; flush, boot, transactional and microcode controls use fixed addresses with enables and locks; entry, machine-check, uncore, turbo, snoop, meter, branch and power registers use fixed addresses.
Debug control provides branch recording among single-bit functions; bank zero uses four consecutive registers for control, status, address and misc, with strided addressing for higher banks.
